sanskrit: naiṣāṃ babhūva saṃprītis tān vicintayatāṃ tadā na rājye na ca nārīṣu na vedādhyayane tathā
english: As they brooded thus, no joy was left in them then—neither in the kingdom, nor in their women, nor in the study of the Vedas.

sanskrit: paraṃ nirvedam agamaṃś cintayanto narādhipam tac ca jñātivadhaṃ ghoraṃ saṃsmarantaḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: They sank into utter despair, dwelling on the king, and recalling again and again that dreadful slaughter of their kinsmen.

sanskrit: abhimanyoś ca bālasya vināśaṃ raṇamūrdhani karṇasya ca mahābāhoḥ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ
english: They remembered the death of the boy Abhimanyu at the forefront of battle, and of the mighty-armed Karṇa, who never fled from combat;

sanskrit: tathaiva draupadeyānām anyeṣāṃ suhṛdām api vadhaṃ saṃsmṛtya te vīrā nātipramanaso 'bhavan
english: and likewise the slaying of the sons of Draupadī and of their other friends—remembering all this, those heroes grew heavy of heart.

sanskrit: hatapravīrāṃ pṛthivīṃ hataratnāṃ ca bhārata sadaiva cintayantas te na nidrām upalebhire
english: Ever brooding, O Bhārata, over the earth bereft of her foremost heroes and stripped of her treasures, they could find no sleep.

sanskrit: draupadī hataputrā ca subhadrā caiva bhāminī nātiprītiyute devyau tadāstām aprahṛṣṭavat
english: Draupadī too, her sons slain, and the radiant Subhadrā—those two ladies remained joyless and unrejoicing.

sanskrit: vairāṭyās tu sutaṃ dṛṣṭvā pitaraṃ te parikṣitam dhārayanti sma te prāṇāṃs tava pūrvapitāmahāḥ
english: Yet, beholding the son of Virāṭa's daughter, your father Parīkṣit, those forefathers of yours clung still to their lives.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ te puruṣavyāghrāḥ pāṇḍavā mātṛnandanāḥ smaranto mātaraṃ vīrā babhūvur bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus those tigers among men, the Pāṇḍavas, delighters of their mother, those heroes, remembering her, became deeply afflicted with grief.

sanskrit: ye rājakāryeṣu purā vyāsaktā nityaśo 'bhavan te rājakāryāṇi tadā nākārṣuḥ sarvataḥ pure
english: They who had once been ever engaged in the affairs of the realm now performed no royal duties anywhere in the city.

sanskrit: āviṣṭā iva śokena nābhyanandanta kiṃ cana saṃbhāṣyamāṇā api te na kiṃ cit pratyapūjayan
english: As though possessed by sorrow, they took pleasure in nothing; even when addressed, they returned no greeting at all.

sanskrit: te sma vīrā durādharṣā gāmbhīrye sāgaropamāḥ śokopahatavijñānā naṣṭasaṃjñā ivābhavan
english: Those heroes, unassailable, like the ocean in their depth, their understanding overwhelmed by grief, became as if bereft of their senses.

sanskrit: anusmaranto jananīṃ tatas te kurunandanāḥ kathaṃ nu vṛddhamithunaṃ vahaty adya pṛthā kṛśā
english: Then those delighters of the Kurus, recalling their mother, mused: How does emaciated Pṛthā now serve that aged couple?

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca sa mahīpālo hataputro nirāśrayaḥ patnyā saha vasaty eko vane śvāpadasevite
english: And how does that lord of the earth, his sons slain, without refuge, dwell alone with his wife in a forest haunted by beasts of prey?

sanskrit: sā ca devī mahābhāgā gāndhārī hatabāndhavā patim andhaṃ kathaṃ vṛddham anveti vijane vane
english: And how does that illustrious lady Gāndhārī, her kinsmen slain, follow her blind and aged husband through the deserted forest?

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ kathayatām autsukyam abhavat tadā gamane cābhavad buddhir dhṛtarāṣṭradidṛkṣayā
english: As they spoke thus, a longing arose in them, and their minds turned toward going, eager to behold Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu rājānaṃ praṇipatyedam abravīt aho me bhavato dṛṣṭaṃ hṛdayaṃ gamanaṃ prati
english: Then Sahadeva, bowing low before the king, said this: Ah, I have read your heart's wish concerning the journey!

sanskrit: na hi tvā gauraveṇāham aśakaṃ vaktum ātmanā gamanaṃ prati rājendra tad idaṃ samupasthitam
english: Out of reverence I could not myself broach to you the matter of this journey, O lord of kings—and now the occasion has come of its own accord.

sanskrit: diṣṭyā drakṣyāmi tāṃ kuntīṃ vartayantīṃ tapasvinīm jaṭilāṃ tāpasīṃ vṛddhāṃ kuśakāśaparikṣatām
english: By good fortune I shall see Kuntī, living the life of an ascetic—matted of hair, an aged hermit-woman, her body scratched by kuśa grass and reeds.

sanskrit: prāsādaharmyasaṃvṛddhām atyantasukhabhāginīm kadā nu jananīṃ śrāntāṃ drakṣyāmi bhṛśaduḥkhitām
english: Reared amid palaces and lofty mansions, the partaker of every comfort—when shall I behold my mother, worn out and sore afflicted?

sanskrit: anityāḥ khalu martyānāṃ gatayo bharatarṣabha kuntī rājasutā yatra vasaty asukhinī vane
english: Truly the fortunes of mortals are fleeting, O bull of the Bhāratas, when Kuntī, a king's daughter, dwells joyless in the forest.

sanskrit: sahadevavacaḥ śrutvā draupadī yoṣitāṃ varā uvāca devī rājānam abhipūjyābhinandya ca
english: Hearing Sahadeva's words, the lady Draupadī, foremost of women, having honored and greeted the king, spoke.

sanskrit: kadā drakṣyāmi tāṃ devīṃ yadi jīvati sā pṛthā jīvantyā hy adya naḥ prītir bhaviṣyati narādhipa
english: When shall I see that noble lady, if Pṛthā yet lives? For if she lives, O lord of men, joy shall come to us this day.

sanskrit: eṣā te 'stu matir nityaṃ dharme te ramatāṃ manaḥ yo 'dya tvam asmān rājendra śreyasā yojayiṣyasi
english: May this resolve of yours endure forever; may your mind ever delight in righteousness, O lord of kings, since this day you will join us to so blessed a thing.

sanskrit: agrapādasthitaṃ cemaṃ viddhi rājan vadhūjanam kāṅkṣantaṃ darśanaṃ kuntyā gāndhāryāḥ śvaśurasya ca
english: Know, O king, that these your daughters-in-law stand ready upon tiptoe, longing to behold Kuntī, Gāndhārī, and our father-in-law.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ sa nṛpo devyā pāñcālyā bharatarṣabha senādhyakṣān samānāyya sarvān idam athābravīt
english: Thus addressed by the Pāñcāla princess, O bull of the Bhāratas, the king summoned all the commanders of his army and spoke to them.

sanskrit: niryātayata me senāṃ prabhūtarathakuñjarām drakṣyāmi vanasaṃsthaṃ ca dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ mahīpatim
english: Lead forth my army, rich in chariots and elephants; I shall go to behold King Dhṛtarāṣṭra, who dwells in the forest.

sanskrit: stryadhyakṣāṃś cābravīd rājā yānāni vividhāni me sajjīkriyantāṃ sarvāṇi śibikāś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: And the king said to the keepers of the women's quarters: Let all my conveyances of every kind be made ready, and palanquins by the thousand.

sanskrit: śakaṭāpaṇaveśāś ca kośaśilpina eva ca niryāntu kośapālāś ca kurukṣetrāśramaṃ prati
english: Let the carts, the market-stalls, the courtesans, the artisans of the treasury, and the keepers of the treasure set out toward the hermitage in Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: yaś ca paurajanaḥ kaś cid draṣṭum icchati pārthivam anāvṛtaḥ suvihitaḥ sa ca yātu surakṣitaḥ
english: And whatever townsman wishes to see the king—unhindered, well-provided, and well-guarded, let him too go forth.

sanskrit: sūdāḥ paurogavāś caiva sarvaṃ caiva mahānasam vividhaṃ bhakṣyabhojyaṃ ca śakaṭair uhyatāṃ mama
english: Let my cooks and stewards, the whole of my kitchen, and food and viands of every sort be carried in the wagons.

sanskrit: prayāṇaṃ ghuṣyatāṃ caiva śvobhūta iti mā ciram kriyantāṃ pathi cāpy adya veśmāni vividhāni ca
english: Let the departure be proclaimed for the morrow—without delay; and let various lodgings be raised along the road this very day.

sanskrit: evam ājñāpya rājā sa bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaḥ śvobhūte niryayau rājā sastrībālapuraskṛtaḥ
english: Having so commanded, that Pāṇḍava king, together with his brothers, set out at break of day, leading forth the women and children before him.

sanskrit: sa bahir divasān evaṃ janaughaṃ paripālayan nyavasan nṛpatiḥ pañca tato 'gacchad vanaṃ prati
english: Thus the king, marshalling the throng of people, encamped outside for five days, and then proceeded toward the forest.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ājñāpayām āsa tataḥ senāṃ bharatasattamaḥ arjunapramukhair guptāṃ lokapālopamair naraiḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then that best of the Bhāratas gave the order to the army, guarded by men led by Arjuna, who were like the guardians of the world.

sanskrit: yogo yoga iti prītyā tataḥ śabdo mahān abhūt krośatāṃ sādināṃ tatra yujyatāṃ yujyatām iti
english: "Yoke up! Yoke up!"—a great glad clamor arose, the riders crying out, "Harness! Harness!"

sanskrit: ke cid yānair narā jagmuḥ ke cid aśvair manojavaiḥ rathaiś ca nagarākāraiḥ pradīptajvalanopamaiḥ
english: Some men went in carriages, some on horses swift as thought, and in chariots vast as cities and blazing like fire.

sanskrit: gajendraiś ca tathaivānye ke cid uṣṭrair narādhipa padātinas tathaivānye nakharaprāsayodhinaḥ
english: Others on lordly elephants, some on camels, O lord of men, and others on foot, fighters armed with claws and spears.

sanskrit: paurajānapadāś caiva yānair bahuvidhais tathā anvayuḥ kururājānaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭradidṛkṣayā
english: The townsmen and country-folk too, in conveyances of many kinds, followed the Kuru king, eager to behold Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sa cāpi rājavacanād ācāryo gautamaḥ kṛpaḥ senām ādāya senānī prayayāv āśramaṃ prati
english: And at the king's word the preceptor Kṛpa of the line of Gautama, as commander, took the host and marched toward the hermitage.

sanskrit: tato dvijair vṛtaḥ śrīmān kururājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saṃstūyamāno bahubhiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ
english: Then the illustrious Kuru king Yudhiṣṭhira, surrounded by brahmins and praised by many bards, heralds, and minstrels,

sanskrit: pāṇḍureṇātapatreṇa dhriyamāṇena mūrdhani rathānīkena mahatā niryayau kurunandanaḥ
english: with a white parasol held above his head, set forth with a great array of chariots, that delighter of the Kurus.

sanskrit: gajaiś cācalasaṃkāśair bhīmakarmā vṛkodaraḥ sajjayantrāyudhopetaiḥ prayayau mārutātmajaḥ
english: And Vṛkodara of terrible deeds, the son of the Wind, marched forth with elephants huge as mountains, equipped with ready engines and weapons.

sanskrit: mādrīputrāv api tathā hayārohaiḥ susaṃvṛtau jagmatuḥ prītijananau saṃnaddhakavacadhvajau
english: The two sons of Mādrī likewise, well-encircled by horsemen, went forth, gladdening to behold, mailed and armed with banners.

sanskrit: arjunaś ca mahātejā rathenādityavarcasā vaśī śvetair hayair divyair yuktenānvagaman nṛpam
english: And Arjuna of great splendor, self-controlled, followed the king in a chariot bright as the sun, yoked with divine white horses.

sanskrit: draupadīpramukhāś cāpi strīsaṃghāḥ śibikāgatāḥ stryadhyakṣayuktāḥ prayayur visṛjanto 'mitaṃ vasu
english: The companies of women too, led by Draupadī, seated in palanquins and attended by their guardians, went forth, scattering boundless wealth.

sanskrit: samṛddhanaranāgāśvaṃ veṇuvīṇānināditam śuśubhe pāṇḍavaṃ sainyaṃ tat tadā bharatarṣabha
english: Abounding in men, elephants, and horses, resounding with flute and lute, that Pāṇḍava host shone resplendent then, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: nadītīreṣu ramyeṣu saratsu ca viśāṃ pate vāsān kṛtvā krameṇātha jagmus te kurupuṃgavāḥ
english: Halting in turn on pleasant riverbanks and beside lakes, O lord of peoples, those foremost of Kurus journeyed onward.

sanskrit: yuyutsuś ca mahātejā dhaumyaś caiva purohitaḥ yudhiṣṭhirasya vacanāt puraguptiṃ pracakratuḥ
english: Yuyutsu of great might and the household priest Dhaumya, by Yudhiṣṭhira's command, undertook the defense of the city.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā kurukṣetram avātarat krameṇottīrya yamunāṃ nadīṃ paramapāvanīm
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, having crossed in due course the most holy river Yamunā, came down into Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: sa dadarśāśramaṃ dūrād rājarṣes tasya dhīmataḥ śatayūpasya kauravya dhṛtarāṣṭrasya caiva ha
english: From afar he beheld the hermitage of the wise royal sage Śatayūpa, O Kaurava, and of Dhṛtarāṣṭra as well.

sanskrit: tataḥ pramuditaḥ sarvo janas tad vanam añjasā viveśa sumahānādair āpūrya bharatarṣabha
english: Then all the people, full of joy, straightway entered that forest, filling it with their mighty shouts, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas te pāṇḍavā dūrād avatīrya padātayaḥ abhijagmur narapater āśramaṃ vinayānatāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the Pāṇḍavas, alighting from afar and going on foot, approached the king's hermitage, bowed low in humility.

sanskrit: sa ca paurajanaḥ sarvo ye ca rāṣṭranivāsinaḥ striyaś ca kurumukhyānāṃ padbhir evānvayus tadā
english: And all the townsfolk, and those who dwelt in the realm, and the women of the chief Kurus, followed then likewise on foot.

sanskrit: āśramaṃ te tato jagmur dhṛtarāṣṭrasya pāṇḍavāḥ śūnyaṃ mṛgagaṇākīrṇaṃ kadalīvanaśobhitam
english: The Pāṇḍavas then came to Dhṛtarāṣṭra's hermitage—deserted, thronged with herds of deer, and graced with groves of plantain.

sanskrit: tatas tatra samājagmus tāpasā vividhavratāḥ pāṇḍavān āgatān draṣṭuṃ kautūhalasamanvitāḥ
english: Then the ascetics of manifold vows gathered there, filled with curiosity to see the Pāṇḍavas who had come.

sanskrit: tān apṛcchat tato rājā kvāsau kauravavaṃśabhṛt pitā jyeṣṭho gato 'smākam iti bāṣpapariplutaḥ
english: Then the king asked them, his eyes brimming with tears: Where has he gone, that upholder of the Kaurava line, our eldest father?

sanskrit: tam ūcus te tato vākyaṃ yamunām avagāhitum puṣpāṇām udakumbhasya cārthe gata iti prabho
english: They answered him with these words: He has gone, O lord, to bathe in the Yamunā, to gather flowers and to fill a water-jar.

sanskrit: tair ākhyātena mārgeṇa tatas te prayayus tadā dadṛśuś cāvidūre tān sarvān atha padātayaḥ
english: Then, by the path the ascetics had shown, they set forth on foot, and before long they saw them all at no great distance.

sanskrit: tatas te satvarā jagmuḥ pitur darśanakāṅkṣiṇaḥ sahadevas tu vegena prādhāvad yena sā pṛthā
english: Then, longing for the sight of their father, they hurried on; and Sahadeva ran swiftly toward where Pṛthā was.

sanskrit: sasvanaṃ prarudan dhīmān mātuḥ pādāv upaspṛśan sā ca bāṣpāvilamukhī pradadarśa priyaṃ sutam
english: Weeping aloud, the wise one touched his mother's feet; and she, her face clouded with tears, beheld her beloved son.

sanskrit: bāhubhyāṃ saṃpariṣvajya samunnāmya ca putrakam gāndhāryāḥ kathayām āsa sahadevam upasthitam
english: Clasping her little son in both arms and raising him up, she announced to Gāndhārī that Sahadeva had arrived.

sanskrit: anantaraṃ ca rājānaṃ bhīmasenam athārjunam nakulaṃ ca pṛthā dṛṣṭvā tvaramāṇopacakrame
english: And next, when Pṛthā saw the king, and Bhīmasena, and Arjuna, and Nakula, she hastened toward them.

sanskrit: sā hy agre 'gacchata tayor daṃpatyor hataputrayoḥ karṣantī tau tatas te tāṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃnyapatan bhuvi
english: She walked ahead of that royal couple whose sons were slain, leading them by the hand; and the brothers, beholding her, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tān rājā svarayogena sparśena ca mahāmanāḥ pratyabhijñāya medhāvī samāśvāsayata prabhuḥ
english: That great-souled, wise king, recognizing them by their voices and by their touch, comforted them, the lord.

sanskrit: tatas te bāṣpam utsṛjya gāndhārīsahitaṃ nṛpam upatasthur mahātmāno mātaraṃ ca yathāvidhi
english: Then those great souls, shedding tears, drew near the king who was with Gāndhārī, and to their mother, with due observance.

sanskrit: sarveṣāṃ toyakalaśāñ jagṛhus te svayaṃ tadā pāṇḍavā labdhasaṃjñās te mātrā cāśvāsitāḥ punaḥ
english: The Pāṇḍavas, recovering their senses and again consoled by their mother, themselves took up the water-jars of all of them.

sanskrit: tato nāryo nṛsiṃhānāṃ sa ca yodhajanas tadā paurajānapadāś caiva dadṛśus taṃ narādhipam
english: Then the women of those lions among men, and the soldiery, and the townsmen and country-folk, looked upon the king.

sanskrit: nivedayām āsa tadā janaṃ taṃ nāmagotrataḥ yudhiṣṭhiro narapatiḥ sa cainān pratyapūjayat
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira presented those people to him by name and lineage, and Dhṛtarāṣṭra returned their salutations.

sanskrit: sa taiḥ parivṛto mene harṣabāṣpāvilekṣaṇaḥ rājātmānaṃ gṛhagataṃ pureva gajasāhvaye
english: Surrounded by them, his eyes clouded with tears of joy, the king felt himself once more at home, as of old in the City of the Elephant.

sanskrit: abhivādito vadhūbhiś ca kṛṣṇādyābhiḥ sa pārthivaḥ gāndhāryā sahito dhīmān kuntyā ca pratyanandata
english: Saluted too by his daughters-in-law, Kṛṣṇā and the rest, that wise king, together with Gāndhārī and Kuntī, greeted them gladly in return.

sanskrit: tataś cāśramam āgacchat siddhacāraṇasevitam didṛkṣubhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ nabhas tārāgaṇair iva
english: Then he came to the hermitage, frequented by siddhas and cāraṇas, thronged with eager onlookers as the sky is crowded with hosts of stars.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa taiḥ saha naravyāghrair bhrātṛbhir bharatarṣabha rājā rucirapadmākṣair āsāṃ cakre tadāśrame
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: In the company of those tigers among men, his brothers, O bull of the Bhāratas, the king with their lovely lotus-eyes took his seat in that hermitage.

sanskrit: tāpasaiś ca mahābhāgair nānādeśasamāgataiḥ draṣṭuṃ kurupateḥ putrān pāṇḍavān pṛthuvakṣasaḥ
english: And with him were illustrious ascetics gathered from many lands, come to see the broad-chested Pāṇḍava sons of the Kuru lord.

sanskrit: te 'bruvañ jñātum icchāmaḥ katamo 'tra yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bhīmārjunayamāś caiva draupadī ca yaśasvinī
english: They said: We wish to learn which one here is Yudhiṣṭhira, and Bhīma, Arjuna, and the twins, and the renowned Draupadī.

sanskrit: tān ācakhyau tadā sūtaḥ sarvān nāmābhināmataḥ saṃjayo draupadīṃ caiva sarvāś cānyāḥ kurustriyaḥ
english: Then the sūta Saṃjaya named them all to the ascetics, each by his name, and Draupadī too, and all the other Kuru women.

sanskrit: ya eṣa jāmbūnadaśuddhagaura;tanur mahāsiṃha iva pravṛddhaḥ pracaṇḍaghoṇaḥ pṛthudīrghanetras; tāmrāyatāsyaḥ kururāja eṣaḥ
english: He whose frame is fair as pure refined gold, full-grown like a great lion, with a high-bridged nose, broad long eyes, and a wide coppery face—this is the Kuru king.

sanskrit: ayaṃ punar mattagajendragāmī; prataptacāmīkaraśuddhagauraḥ pṛthvāyatāṃsaḥ pṛthudīrghabāhur; vṛkodaraḥ paśyata paśyatainam
english: And this one, who moves with the gait of a rutting lordly elephant, fair as refined and tempered gold, with broad wide shoulders and long thick arms—this is Vṛkodara: behold him, behold him!

sanskrit: yas tv eṣa pārśve 'sya mahādhanuṣmāñ; śyāmo yuvā vāraṇayūthapābhaḥ siṃhonnatāṃso gajakhelagāmī; padmāyatākṣo 'rjuna eṣa vīraḥ
english: He who stands at his side, the great bowman, dark and youthful, splendid as the leader of an elephant herd, his shoulders high as a lion's, moving with an elephant's sport, his eyes wide as lotus-petals—this hero is Arjuna.

sanskrit: kuntīsamīpe puruṣottamau tu; yamāv imau viṣṇumahendrakalpau manuṣyaloke sakale samo 'sti; yayor na rūpe na bale na śīle
english: And beside Kuntī, these two foremost of men, the twins, are like Viṣṇu and great Indra; in all the world of men there is none equal to them in beauty, in strength, or in character.

sanskrit: iyaṃ punaḥ padmadalāyatākṣī; madhyaṃ vayaḥ kiṃ cid iva spṛśantī nīlotpalābhā puradevateva; kṛṣṇā sthitā mūrtimatīva lakṣmīḥ
english: And this one, her eyes wide as lotus-petals, just touching upon middle age, with the luster of the blue lotus, like the tutelary goddess of the city—this is Kṛṣṇā, standing there like Lakṣmī made flesh.
